metadata.title: Using machine learning algorithms to predict students’ general self-efficacy in PISA 2018

design_fields.q1_rationale: The study does not use PISA achievement plausible values for the outcome, which indicates that it does not meet the criteria for proper handling of plausible values.
design_fields.q2_rationale: Recorded evidence does not explicitly establish an unweighted analysis. Original extraction rationale: The study uses publicly available PISA 2018 microdata but does not mention applying any sampling or replicate weights in the analysis.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The study does not provide information indicating that it used multilevel modeling or accounted for school clustering in its analysis.
design_fields.q4_rationale: The study does not mention any external validation strategies and appears to rely solely on internal validation methods.
design_fields._pdf_matched: 107. Tan et al. (2025). Using machine learning algorithms to predict students’ general self-efficacy in PISA 2018.pdf
design_fields.q4b_note: LLM (gpt-5.4-nano): We then used two machine learning algorithms, Lasso and XGBoost, to predict self-efficacy of 612,004 students aged 15 to 16 years from 79 countries and regions. The results showed that XGBoost outperformed Lasso.
design_fields._q2_audit: Corrected not_met to not_reported because original rationale reports absence of weight information or an inference, not direct evidence of unweighted analysis; source verification still required.
